summary: This Dockerfile builds a Ubuntu container pre-configured for demonstrating git worktree workflows. It installs development tools (git, zsh, vim, fzf), sets up a sample git repository with a feature branch mid-refactor, creates a bare remote repository to simulate GitHub, and installs a custom zsh function called `gwt` that lets you interactively navigate between git worktrees using fuzzy search.

explanations.3: This tells Docker to run installation commands without prompting for user input, since there's no interactive terminal in a container.
explanations.7: The sed command modifies Ubuntu's package source configuration to unlock additional repositories (universe and multiverse) where less common packages like fzf live.
explanations.15: After installing packages, we delete the cached package lists to reduce the final image size since we won't need to install anything else.
explanations.24: This creates a bare git repository (one without a working directory) that acts like a remote server on GitHub, so the later `git push` commands have a real destination.
explanations.29: We're creating the directory structure and files that will exist in the demo repository — three source files that represent a partially-refactored project.
explanations.33:
The `printf` command writes multi-line text into files; the `
` creates newlines so each file contains valid JavaScript/TypeScript code.
explanations.42: After committing the initial code to main, we create and switch to a new branch called feature/user-notifications where we'll simulate in-progress work.
explanations.43: These lines rewrite two of the files on the feature branch to show what a refactor in progress looks like (the code is changed but not yet committed).
explanations.52:
The printf with multiple '%s
' arguments is a way to write many lines of text at once; each quoted string becomes one line in the output.
explanations.71: The `awk '{print $1}'` extracts just the first column (the path) from the git worktree list output, ignoring the branch name and other info.
explanations.75: This constructs a directory name by taking the top-level git repository path and appending the branch name with slashes converted to hyphens.
explanations.87: The `>>` appends these lines to the zshrc file (instead of `>` which would overwrite), adding the function to the shell's autoload path so it's available as a command.
explanations.94: The `-i` flag makes the shell interactive (so you can type commands), and `-l` makes it a login shell (so it loads all configuration files).
